note: Rewritten from Hagen 1858. The original entry for this species consists of a Latin diagnosis (Smeathman's original text and Fabricius's description of Termes arda standing side by side) plus German remarks (Monographie der Termiten, no. 43 Termes atrox Smeathman, Smeathman, Philos. Transact. vol. 71, p. 141, no. 3, Tab. 10, fig. 14–18; Tab. 9). The distribution is given as "equatorial Africa (Sierra Leone)", consistent with the type locality on the entry page; the original also records its nest as a conical clay nest 2—3 feet high, with a rounded dome and a complete, projecting rim, mixed with grass stems. Measurements: body length 9 mm; length with wings 17 mm; wingspan 31 mm (Smeathman's original gives a wingspan of 1 1/2 inches); larva 5 mm; soldier 8—13 mm (all from the original figures). Hagen suspected that this species is in fact a Eutermes close to T. arborum. The original uses soldier-form nymphs with forked mandibles and worker-form larvae as the caste descriptions; this entry merges them under soldier and worker. OCR errors (Terraes, atris, antennig, productp, nulüs, etc.) have been read against the context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Smaller than the preceding species, black, the margins of each abdominal segment pale (white); the wings lie flat on the back and are black; all the legs are pale earth-coloured. Original Latin description: nearly black, the margins of the abdominal segments pale, antennae and legs earth-coloured, wings smoky, costa black, the ocelli situated below, with a dot-like depression in the centre. Fabricius described it separately (Termes arda): black, the apex of the abdominal segments pale, legs pale. Hagen states that he himself never saw the alate of this species, and from Smeathman's original figure points out that its ocelli are large and far from the compound eyes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The original, following Smeathman's figure and description, records it as puppa militans (soldier-form nymph): the head is very large and earth-coloured, raised in front into a hump, oval behind, blunt and produced; the mandibles project forward, are forked and black; the antennae are moniliform, earth-coloured and as long as the head; there are no eyes (blind); the thorax is small, the abdomen oval and lead-grey; the legs are earth-coloured. Measurements: body length (from the original figure) 8—13 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Recorded in the original as larva operaria (worker-form larva): the head is pale, the antennae moniliform, the eyes absent (blind), the mandibles short and toothed; the thorax and abdomen are oval and lead-grey; the legs are pale (given as earth-coloured in Entom. syst.). Measurements: body length 5 mm.
